To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cytotoxic T cell precursor frequency is low but measurable in the spleens of newborn mice, and increases with age.
the development of cell mediated immunity in mice is a complex process that begins in the fetus, continues after birth, and is dependent on the interaction of several cell types and factors.
Cytotoxic T-cell development occurs in the spleen of postnatal mice, and is not detectable in newborn mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of immune responses during the first 3 weeks after birth, a period of rapid growth and maturation.
the ontogeny of the immune system.
the development of cell-mediated immune reactivity in mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ontogeny of the immune system is not as complex as it was previously thought.
the ontogeny of T-cell functions is not as well developed as the ontogeny and development of humoral responses.
cell-mediated immune functions are not present in spleen cells of newborn mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
all of the major components of cell-mediated immune responses are present at birth, although the response of the newborn mouse may be suppressed by a factor or factors which disappear with time.
all cell-mediated immune functions are present in the newborn mouse, but are not fully developed until the second postnatal week of age.
the development of cell-mediated immune responses occurs in the postnatal mouse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune system is not fully functional until 12 days after the neonate is born.
the development of cell-mediated immunity is a complex, multifactorial event.
the development of the immune response is a complex process that is not restricted to a single cell type.
